heuristic_statement: Historical requirements audit operates on an evidential separation of three tiers: primary ground truth (executable code, workflow definitions, deterministic tests, and persisted runtime artifacts), normative specification (Agents.md and configuration files), and secondary historical narrative (git logs and commit summaries). A surviving requirement is defined as any requirement established across the project's historical arc whose core intent has neither been explicitly revoked nor superseded by subsequent normative directives or active runtime architecture. Supersession is determined chronologically and structurally: subsequent specification updates, architecture overhauls, or explicit user counter-instructions retire earlier requirements without imposing present corrective obligation. Conversely, any surviving requirement absent from, partially implemented in, or contradictory to today's active executable code (send-to-gemini.js, active workflows, step-3 evaluation heuristic) constitutes an outstanding gap.

completeness_strategy.coverage_invariants: Every segment SEG-00001 through SEG-00157 is allocated to exactly one primary batch, yielding 100% primary coverage with 0 bytes unassigned or duplicated across the primary tier. Crosscheck batches selectively duplicate high-authority runtime specifications, git historical transitions, and representative run executions within a strict budget of <= 1,440,000 bytes, well below the 6,458,895-byte ceiling. All evaluators execute in isolated, fresh processes consuming strictly bounded payloads.
completeness_strategy.synthesis_balancing: Primary and crosscheck evaluation outputs are partitioned into four balanced quartiles (Q1-Q4) by serialized result volume, reduced into dyads (D1=Q1+Q2, D2=Q3+Q4), and finalized into the comprehensive audit record without context leakage or historical raw corpus reintroduction.
